3.3 Narrative Exception / Historical Conflict Register
Issue	Locked narration	Evidence conflict	Production decision
Air-assault brigade identity	31st Guards Air Assault Brigade + 45th Separate Guards Special Purpose Brigade, phrased “understood to have included”	Newer MWI/Canadian/WOTR support 31st+45th; earlier MWI identifies 11th+45th.	Keep locked wording; do not render decisive readable 31st badge/patch; internal shot evidence stays DISPUTED.
Helicopter loss count	“several are lost, although published loss totals differ”	Contemporary/retrospective estimates differ materially.	Never show a neat comprehensive loss ledger; individual loss beats represent documented friction without asserting total.
Il-76 scale	18 reported heading toward Kyiv; wider prepared force up to 41 / 4,000	Figures refer to different scopes rather than necessarily competing totals.	Visualize visible subsets and explicitly state historical context in prompts; do not show 41 aircraft simultaneously as if all airborne.
Il-76 abort	Multi-causal likely factors	Sources differ on runway damage, insecurity, aircraft-loss risk and surviving air defence.	No single visual says “one crater stops the mission”; montage/shot chain carries combined risk.
Overnight control	Ukrainian push back into airport area; exact control disputed	Later accounts differ in description of retaking/withdrawal and sector control.	Dusk shot uses uncertain control-state geometry, no clean flag-raising or total-ownership image.
“NATO codename Candid” wording	Locked exactly as supplied by user	Standard technical phrasing is generally “NATO reporting name,” but user explicitly locked the narration after declining that change.	Preserve N001 verbatim. Production notes may use technical nomenclature without altering VO.

3.4 HCP001 — Kyiv Oblast / Hostomel, 24–27 February 2022
Environment: cold-season Kyiv Oblast; winter-bare deciduous trees and subdued vegetation; damp/dark earth and concrete plausible; no default snow blanket.
Airport: large industrial/test-flight airfield, long concrete runway, apron, major hangars, perimeter/woods; no generic NATO airbase furniture or invented Western ground equipment.
Russian aviation: Ka-52, Mi-8 family and Mi-24 family only where evidence supports; no Mi-28/Tiger/Apache substitutions; no modern Il-76MD-90A substitution for classic Il-76MD family.
Russian assault personnel: 2022-era VDV/special-purpose material culture at representative family level. Unit-badge microdetail is not used to resolve the 31st-vs-11th conflict.
Ukrainian defenders: National Guard 4th Rapid Reaction Brigade residual garrison, small arms, ZU-23-2 and Igla-family MANPADS; no Western post-invasion kit by default in opening-morning shots.
Ukrainian counterattack: elements, not whole brigades, from 72nd Mechanized, 80th and 95th Air Assault and 3rd Special Purpose/SOF; separate groups are used to avoid false massing.
Effects: real muzzle flashes, flare burn, rotor wash, localized artillery impact, smoke/fire ownership. No game tracers, shockwave rings, universal turret tosses, giant fuel-air fireballs or endless explosions.
Human presentation: restrained task-focused behaviour, no celebratory posing, no gore, no theatrical reaction faces, no civilians inserted into combat frames unless explicitly evidenced and narratively required.
4. Narrative Thesis, Viewer Promise & Runtime Architecture
CENTRAL DRAMATIC QUESTION: Can Russia turn a successful helicopter insertion at Antonov into the functioning airhead required for a rapid move on Kyiv?
THESIS: Russia can seize and later hold the airport, but possession of Antonov is not the same thing as opening the planned Il-76 air bridge. Ukrainian resistance, fires, air attack, counterattack, residual air-defence threat and instability deny the operational payoff. The story ends with the airport in Russian hands but the fight transferred to the roads and river barriers toward Kyiv.
VIEWER PROMISE: By the cliffhanger, the viewer will understand exactly why Hostomel mattered, how the helicopter assault unfolded, why the follow-on airlift failed to materialize, how Russian ground forces still secured the airport, and why Part 2 must be a ground battle through Bucha and Irpin rather than a continuation of the first-day airhead plan.

00:22–01:12	Launch / defenders	S004–S012	Bolshoy Bokov -> package -> troops -> small garrison -> air defence
01:12–01:56	Ingress	S013–S018	Low reservoir flight -> dam -> hit -> flares -> turn west -> defenders hear rotors
01:56–03:28	Air assault	S019–S031	Suppression -> two lifts -> dismount -> resistance -> withdrawal -> exposed foothold
03:28–03:58	Il-76 threat	S032–S035	Heavy transports -> 18 reported -> wider 41/4,000 prepared package -> operational stakes
03:58–05:30	Airhead denied	S036–S049	D-30 -> impacts -> Su-24 -> counterattack -> insecure LZ -> damage -> residual AD -> Il-76 turnback
05:30–06:16	Night / road link-up	S050–S057	Pushback -> disputed night -> columns -> 25 Feb link-up -> continuing artillery/clashes
06:16–07:42	Captured airport / cliffhanger	S058–S064	Mriya -> destruction -> Russian hold -> absent Il-76 -> road to Bucha/Irpin/Kyiv

6. N001 — Locked Voiceover Master Script
STATUS: LOCKED. No silent wording change is authorised. Evidence mapping is carried by the research dossier and shot contracts.
24–27 February 2022
24 February 2022. Russia's attack on Kyiv begins with a helicopter force moving south from Belarus toward Antonov Airport at Hostomel, roughly thirty kilometres northwest of central Kyiv. Its concrete runway is 3,500 metres long and 56 metres wide, built to handle the heaviest transport aircraft. The plan is to seize the airfield by helicopter, establish an airhead, then fly in a much larger airborne force for a rapid move on the capital.
The assault stages from Bolshoy Bokov airfield in Belarus, roughly 170 kilometres away. Around 09:30, a force of roughly three dozen helicopters crosses into Ukraine. Kamov Ka-52 Alligator attack helicopters and Mil Mi-24 Hind gunships support Mil Mi-8 Hip transports carrying the assault troops.
The landing force is understood to have included elements of the 31st Guards Air Assault Brigade and the 45th Separate Guards Special Purpose Brigade. Both belong to Russia's Airborne Forces — the Vozdushno-desantnye voyska, commonly abbreviated VDV.
At Antonov Airport, fewer than two hundred personnel of Ukraine's 4th Rapid Reaction Brigade of the National Guard defend the airfield. Most of the brigade's combat strength has already deployed elsewhere, leaving a comparatively small force at the airport. Their weapons include rifles, machine guns, Igla-family MANPADS — man-portable air-defense systems — and at least one ZU-23-2 twin 23-millimetre anti-aircraft gun.
The Russian helicopters fly at very low altitude along the Kyiv Reservoir and Dnipro approach. Near the Kyiv hydroelectric dam at Vyshhorod, the formation comes under fire. Lead helicopters are hit. Aircraft behind them release flares, break and continue west toward Hostomel.
By around 11:00, the assault reaches the airport. Ka-52s and Mi-24s suppress Ukrainian positions while the Mi-8 transports push toward the landing areas. Two successive lifts of ten Mi-8s each put roughly three hundred Russian VDV and special-purpose troops onto Antonov.
The soldiers dismount and spread away from the helicopters toward the apron, runway, airport buildings and perimeter. Ukrainian defenders continue firing from positions around the airfield. Russian helicopters are hit and several are lost, although published loss totals differ. The landing continues.
The Ukrainian National Guard defenders hold for roughly two hours. Ammunition begins running critically low and they withdraw from the immediate airfield. By early afternoon, the Russian assault force has a foothold at Antonov.
But the troops delivered by helicopter are lightly equipped and have no substantial armored force or artillery with them. Capturing the runway is only the first half of the operation.
The next echelon is supposed to arrive by Ilyushin Il-76 heavy transports, NATO codename Candid. The Pskov-based 76th Guards Air Assault Division is understood to have formed the principal follow-on force. Eighteen Il-76s are reported heading toward Kyiv. The wider force being prepared for the operation is understood to have included as many as forty-one transports carrying up to four thousand troops.
If those aircraft reach Antonov, the relatively small helicopter landing can become a major airborne bridgehead on the outskirts of the Ukrainian capital.
Ukraine moves before that can happen. Artillery begins striking Antonov. The fires are understood to have included 122-millimetre D-30 towed howitzers from the 4th Rapid Reaction Brigade, used against the runway. Ukrainian Su-24 strike aircraft also attack the airfield.
At the same time, a larger Ukrainian counterattack is assembled from forces around Kyiv. It includes elements of the 72nd Separate Mechanized Brigade, the 80th and 95th Air Assault Brigades and the 3rd Separate Special Purpose Regiment of Ukraine's Special Operations Forces. By late afternoon these units are moving back toward Hostomel.
Fighting returns to the runway, apron, airport buildings and surrounding treelines. The Russian assault force now has to hold the ground it seized while Ukrainian artillery continues reaching the airfield and Ukrainian troops close on the perimeter.
Antonov is no longer a secure transport landing zone. The runway has been damaged. Russian control on the ground remains unstable. Ukrainian forces are counterattacking. Surviving air-defense weapons still threaten large, slow transport aircraft approaching the airport.
The precise reason the transport mission is finally cancelled remains disputed. Runway damage, the insecure ground situation and the continuing threat to the Il-76s are all likely factors. But the operational result is clear - the transport force turns back and the intended air bridge never opens.
By late on 24 February, Ukrainian forces have pushed back into the airport area and the original Russian helicopter assault force can no longer provide the secure airhead required by the plan. Exact control of every part of Antonov during the night remains disputed, but the central fact does not: the heavy follow-on force has not landed.
Russian ground columns are already moving south from Belarus. The helicopter force has failed to open the planned air bridge, but another Russian force is approaching Hostomel by road.
On 25 February, those ground forces reach the airport and link with the airborne troops. Armored and mechanized forces secure Antonov Airport again. Russia has recovered the airfield — but by road, not through the rapid aerial reinforcement operation intended on the first morning.
The fighting around Antonov does not stop straight away. Ukrainian artillery continues striking Russian positions. Clashes persist around the perimeter, nearby woods and approaches. Ukrainian official accounts describe fighting for control of the airport continuing intermittently through 27 February.
During this period, the Antonov An-225 Mriya is destroyed inside its hangar. The world's largest operational aircraft now lies wrecked at an airport Russia had intended to turn into the aerial gateway to Kyiv.
By the end of 27 February, Russia holds Antonov Airport. But the air bridge it was captured to create has never materialized. The Il-76 follow-on force has not landed. The rapid airborne shortcut into Kyiv has disappeared.
Russia still holds Hostomel. Thousands of Russian troops are still moving south from Belarus. And the Ukrainian capital is still only a short distance away.
But reaching it now requires a completely different battle.
The helicopter assault has given Russia a foothold at Hostomel. But from here, the advance must continue on the ground — through Bucha, toward Irpin, across the river barriers and into the defended northwestern approaches to Kyiv.
The battle for the airhead is over.
The battle for the road to Kyiv is about to begin.

8. STY001 — Master Visual Style Bible
Render as an unambiguously real live-action photographic frame made by a physical camera in late-February Kyiv Oblast. Materials must read as actual painted metal, rubber, glass, fabric, wet concrete, damp soil, winter vegetation and human skin, not game-engine PBR or illustration. Preserve natural highlight roll-off, ordinary optical imperfections, plausible depth of field, atmospheric extinction, restrained colour, realistic black levels and exposure. Weather is a researched or bounded state variable rather than decoration. Do not add arbitrary orange/teal grading, synthetic volumetric glow, excessive HDR, perfect procedural terrain, glossy armour/aircraft, impossible rim light, floating camera behaviour, generated captions, UI, watermarks or invented readable text.
Photographic truth hierarchy: historical/physical truth -> material truth -> environmental truth -> photographic response -> creative cinematography.
Cinematography may be sophisticated, but executable render prompts do not use “epic”, “blockbuster”, “CGI render”, “Unreal”, “concept art”, “game-cinematic” or similar synthetic rendering adjectives.
Camera behaviour is conditional. Use stable observation where geography/tension matters, shoulder observation for human immediacy, measured tracking/panning for movement, and elevated geography only when physically plausible.
One dominant visual event plus one dominant camera idea per shot. Do not overload combat with independent simultaneous actions that invite duplication/fusion.
Light/weather changes only because chronology/weather changes. The project does not impose one destructive global grade on morning, afternoon, dusk and interior/hangar states.
All generated historical shots are image-only. Titles, labels, route lines, unit names and explanatory map text are added in post.
8A. Project Photographic Reference Pack / Look Regimes
Look ID	Authority	Use	Lock
STY_DAY	A006 Hostomel Winter Day Look	24 Feb day exterior, airport, reservoir and counterattack daylight	Cold neutral/diffuse daylight; restrained saturation; real wet/damp materials; no default snow.
STY_DUSK	A007 Hostomel Late-Afternoon / Dusk Look	late 24 Feb and final cliffhanger where chronology permits	Natural lowering luminance and cooler sky response; no stylized blue monochrome or golden hour.
STY_AM25	A038 25 February Cold Morning Hostomel State	ground-link-up sequence	Cold morning regional reconstruction; continuity with existing wetness/damage.
STY_HANGAR	A003/A004/A005 + active exterior state	Mriya/hangar views	Interior/covered hangar exposure balanced to real exterior; no theatrical spotlighting.

9. Continuity Framework
Persistent state is treated as data. The selected treatment for each family writes the actual CL state. B/C/D alternatives begin from the same family start state and must reach a history-compatible terminal state; only the treatment selected for edit becomes the default state authority for the next family.
Ledger	Tracks	Persistence rule
CL-AIR	AC01+ recurring aircraft identities	heading, altitude/speed state, damage, landing/door/gear state; damaged aircraft cannot reappear intact as the same AC-ID
CL-RWY	runway surface/damage/obstruction	craters/debris stay in fixed zones and age; runway never rotates/mirrors
CL-FX	smoke/fire/flare sources	unique owner, age, expansion and wind drift
CL-PERS	Russian/Ukrainian subgroups	zone, task, posture, movement direction; groups cannot teleport or swap sides
CL-LIGHT	weather/light/wetness	look regime, cloud, wind, wetness and time progression
CL-CONTROL	airfield control state	sector-level uncertainty allowed; no false neat control map on disputed night

9.1 Airport local world coordinates
Production origin = midpoint of runway 15/33. +X = southeast along runway 15 at approximately 154.9° true. -X = northwest toward runway 33 at approximately 334.0°. +Y = northeast perpendicular to runway. -Y = southwest. +Z = altitude/height AGL. Zones: RWY-NW, RWY-C, RWY-SE, APRON, HANGAR, PER-N, PER-S, WOOD-W, ROAD-E. Coordinates are continuity controls, not claims that public records fix every soldier or helicopter to a metre.
10. Director-Level Master Shot List, Evidence Registers & Scene Topology
The shot list is the film’s authoring blueprint. Every family below has four executable treatments with the same historical beat and terminal truth but meaningfully different camera logic. A is canonical; B uses longer-lens/standoff logic; C changes scale toward human/technical observation; D is a premium offset/elevated safety solution. Exact local prompts later expand every treatment independently.

10.1 Shot Evidence Micro-Register — family rulings
S001 Family — Antonov Before the Assault
STORY/HISTORICAL FUNCTION: Operational geography: Hostomel lies northwest of Kyiv and the airport is the objective. PARENT: SC001 / SEQ001. EVIDENCE MICRO-REGISTER: use R001; R010. REQUIRED ASSETS: A001, A003, A006. COUNT/GEOMETRY: exact visible count is declared by the local S treatment; where the shot represents a larger historical package it must state VISIBLE SUBSET versus historical context. CAMERA VARIANTS: A — Canonical director treatment balancing geography, subject readability and editorial continuity with a physically plausible real camera. B — Longer-lens alternative from greater distance, using compression and foreground occlusion to create a meaningfully different but continuity-safe view. 11.1 Dependency / generation order
Tier 1 first: A001, A006, A007, A008, A009, A038, A041, A042. Approve geography/look before dependent narrative assets.
Tier 2 identities next: aircraft, weapons, personnel and recurring vehicles. Critical surface views must exist before shots expose them.
Tier 3 state/effect assets derive from approved parent identities/environments; damage never becomes an accidental new identity.
Tier 4 planning/transition authorities are generated only after the shot plan fixes exactly what they must control.
GATE 1 occurs only after all planned A001–A046 authorities are generated, normalized and QC-passed. No S treatment is generated before Gate 1.

11B. Rights / Marking Register
EXTERNAL_PUBLIC_DOMAIN_REFERENCES = OFF, so no external image is automatically imported into the generation pipeline. Historical research may inform factual configuration, but generation references must be project-approved. CAUTIOUS_CONTEXTUAL marking mode applies: ordinary factual tactical identifiers may appear only when established; distinctive badges/logos receive contextual screening. Because assault-unit attribution is source-conflicted, prominent readable brigade badges are unnecessary and should not be invented.

A001 — Antonov Airport Master Geometry — FULL ASSET MEGAPROMPT
ASSET ID: A001 | TITLE: Antonov Airport Master Geometry
CLASS: Environment / Geography Authority
PRESENTATION MODE: ENVIRONMENT_PLATE
RESEARCH AUTHORITIES: SRC001,SRC015
OUTPUT BACKGROUND / CONTEXT: historically/geographically appropriate environment plate; no unrelated dramatic action
FLOW ASSET TITLE DIRECTIVE: "A001 - Antonov Airport Master Geometry"
FILE-SAFE SLUG: A001_antonov_airport_master_geometry
MUST KEEP / NON-NEGOTIABLE. 1) A001 is the canonical Antonov Airport Master Geometry authority for this project. 2) Function/class: Environment / Geography Authority; presentation mode: ENVIRONMENT_PLATE. 3) Research authorities: SRC001,SRC015. 4) Immutable airport geometry: runway 15/33, 3,500 x 56 m, apron/hangar/perimeter relationships, north-up and local-coordinate authority. 5) Output in full colour as real photographed physical reality, not illustration/CGI. 6) No unsupported exact serial, badge, tail number, weapon load or transient state. 7) No superimposed labels, captions, borders, UI or watermark unless this is intentionally a planning diagram; audience-facing maps still keep labels for post. 8) Do not approve as _FINAL unless every property assigned to this authority is legible and internally coherent.
PURPOSE AND AUTHORITY SCOPE. Create a production-grade reusable reference for Antonov Airport Master Geometry. Immutable airport geometry: runway 15/33, 3,500 x 56 m, apron/hangar/perimeter relationships, north-up and local-coordinate authority. This asset is not a narrative shot. Its purpose is to make downstream generations more accurate and more consistent by owning specific identity, geometry, material, state, geography, technical or photographic information. Keep information outside that authority scope neutral so it cannot contaminate later prompts.
HISTORICAL / TECHNICAL CONFIGURATION. Use the narrowest defensible 24–27 February 2022 configuration. Preserve period-correct construction, proportions, equipment family, paint/camouflage boundaries, antennas/sensors, visible mechanical interfaces and operational state only where supported. Do not upgrade Russian or Ukrainian equipment with later-war accessories by default. For an aircraft/vehicle/weapon authority, show enough angles or detail to establish every surface likely to be revealed later. For an environment authority, inherit A001-style cardinal consistency and make buildings, surfaces, vegetation and horizon physically continuous. For effects/state assets, make the initiating source and persistence rules explicit.
COLOUR, MATERIAL AND SURFACE. Use actual material response: painted metal, composite, rubber, optical glass, canvas/webbing, concrete, soil and vegetation should each behave differently under diffuse winter light. Weathering should be plausible for an operational 2022 system, neither pristine showroom nor fantasy ruin. Preserve factual camouflage colours independently of the photographic look.
REFERENCE CLEANLINESS. Reference-authority doctrine: this output becomes a downstream truth authority only after visual QC. It must be clean enough that later image/video generations can read the property it controls at useful scale. Do not contaminate an identity master with unrelated scenery, dramatic smoke, arbitrary colour cast or shot-specific damage. Where exact historical configuration is unresolved, show the narrowest defensible family and use angle/distance/occlusion to avoid manufacturing a false exact answer. The asset must support later real-world photography, not look like a catalogue render: real material roughness, physically plausible seams, fasteners, wear and construction are essential. Any factual marking that is not established should be absent, unreadable, occluded or generic only when historically defensible; do not invent a plausible-looking serial.
CAMERA / PRESENTATION. Choose the camera geometry that maximizes downstream reference usefulness rather than drama. Object references should use even, restrained light and a lens that does not distort proportions; a 70–105 mm full-frame-equivalent perspective is preferred for isolated identity views, with additional front/side/rear three-quarter views where the selected presentation mode requires them. Environment plates should use an elevated or ground perspective explicitly suited to geography, with north/axis recorded where applicable. Keep required extremities, rotor discs, gun trails, landing gear and antennas inside frame.
TEXT / MARKING POLICY. No invented readable writing. Known factual functional markings may be represented only when evidence closes them and the authority role requires them. Distinctive badges/insignia should remain low-salience unless verified and needed. Unit attribution conflicts must never be resolved through fabricated patches.
MODEL-INFERENCE REGISTER. IDENTITY: NONE except where the asset title intentionally names a family rather than subtype. COUNT: ONE canonical subject or explicitly declared multi-view/formation subset. TECHNICAL CONFIGURATION: bounded by authorities. COLOUR/MARKINGS: researched or intentionally non-specific. SPATIAL ORIENTATION: controlled by presentation. HUMAN TASKING: N/A unless crew/character asset, then explicitly task-neutral or operationally justified. TERRAIN/SITE: controlled for environment assets. CAMERA GEOMETRY: controlled. LIGHTING: controlled. TEXT: no invented text. CONTINUITY: base authority state only. PERMITTED MODEL INTERPRETATION: microscopic scratches, tiny soil/gravel distribution, natural fabric folds and other non-consequential texture.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Verify silhouette/proportions, period configuration, reference cleanliness, colour/material realism, absence of unsupported precise identifiers, absence of AI text, absence of game-engine sheen, correct count, useful reveal coverage, and no conflicts with the research note. Any failed high-consequence property prevents _FINAL promotion.
REFERENCE AND EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Use only the authorities declared for A001 Antonov Airport Master Geometry reusable authority. A source-linked fact controls only the property it actually establishes. When a technical source describes a platform family but not the specific Hostomel aircraft, use it for geometry/performance bounds only, never as evidence for the battle loadout. When a military reconstruction supplies a time, count or route, preserve its confidence classification. When accounts conflict, prefer visual ambiguity and record the conflict rather than merging incompatible claims. The picture should communicate the narrative beat without pretending that every background individual, exact serial, weapon load, firing point or vehicle mix is known.
SPATIAL READABILITY. Build A001 Antonov Airport Master Geometry reusable authority as a physical blocking problem, not an atmospheric collage. Foreground, midground and background must have intentional depth. Keep the dominant subject readable at first glance and allow the second read to reveal the relevant tactical or technical relationship. Use measurable ranges where they prevent model drift, but avoid centimeter-level pseudo-precision. Maintain safe negative space around moving rotors, people, weapons and vehicles. Never place major objects simply because they fill an empty patch of frame; every authenticity-significant object must have an operational reason to be present.
PHOTOGRAPHIC REALITY. Render as an unambiguously real live-action photographic frame made by a physical camera in late-February Kyiv Oblast. Materials must read as actual painted metal, rubber, glass, fabric, wet concrete, damp soil, winter vegetation and human skin, not game-engine PBR or illustration. Preserve natural highlight roll-off, ordinary optical imperfections, plausible depth of field, atmospheric extinction, restrained colour, realistic black levels and exposure. Weather is a researched or bounded state variable rather than decoration. Do not add arbitrary orange/teal grading, synthetic volumetric glow, excessive HDR, perfect procedural terrain, glossy armour/aircraft, impossible rim light, floating camera behaviour, generated captions, UI, watermarks or invented readable text.
HUMAN / OPERATIONAL REALITY. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
PHYSICS / EFFECTS REALITY. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground.
CONTINUITY AND UNCERTAINTY. Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
QUALITY FAILURE FIREBREAK. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
PRE-FLIGHT. Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.

PHYSICS / EFFECTS REALITY. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. CONTINUITY AND UNCERTAINTY. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.

Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground.
CONTINUITY AND UNCERTAINTY. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.

Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground.
CONTINUITY AND UNCERTAINTY. Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
QUALITY FAILURE FIREBREAK. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
PRE-FLIGHT. Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.

Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground.
CONTINUITY AND UNCERTAINTY. Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.

PHYSICS / EFFECTS REALITY. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground.
CONTINUITY AND UNCERTAINTY. Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.

No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
PHYSICS / EFFECTS REALITY. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground.
CONTINUITY AND UNCERTAINTY. Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.

NARRATION LINK (LOCKED; DO NOT REWRITE): 24 February 2022. Russia's attack on Kyiv begins with a helicopter force moving south from Belarus toward Antonov Airport at Hostomel, roughly thirty kilometres northwest of central Kyiv. Its concrete runway is 3,500 metres long and 56 metres wide, built to handle the heaviest transport aircraft. The plan is to seize the airfield by helicopter, establish an airhead, then fly in a much larger airborne force for a rapid move on the capital.

NARRATION LINK (LOCKED; DO NOT REWRITE): 24 February 2022. Russia's attack on Kyiv begins with a helicopter force moving south from Belarus toward Antonov Airport at Hostomel, roughly thirty kilometres northwest of central Kyiv. Its concrete runway is 3,500 metres long and 56 metres wide, built to handle the heaviest transport aircraft. The plan is to seize the airfield by helicopter, establish an airhead, then fly in a much larger airborne force for a rapid move on the capital.

Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL001. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.

When accounts conflict, prefer visual ambiguity and record the conflict rather than merging incompatible claims. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.

END camera position remains within a physically reachable path over 6 seconds and preserves the action axis.
SUBJECT MOTION / SPEED / MECHANICS. Aircraft-motion control: define a single coherent heading and flight state for every visible aircraft. For the low-level ingress sequences, use a production estimate of roughly 10–30 m AGL over open water/flat terrain and a visually credible transit range around 180–240 km/h unless the shot is landing, flaring, turning, damaged or otherwise requires a different bounded state; these values are cinematic/physical staging estimates, not claims of measured combat telemetry. Keep rotor discs physically clear: no intersecting rotor volumes, no air-show wingtip proximity, no cloned spacing. Use staggered longitudinal and lateral separation so each aircraft has wake/rotor safety margin and the viewer can read the package. Bank and pitch must correspond to the commanded turn or speed change. Door, landing-gear and troop-egress states change only for a physical reason. Rotor blur should be photographically plausible rather than frozen or turned into transparent discs. Any damaged aircraft must follow an inertial, aerodynamically plausible path and must not explode simply because it is hit.
ENTITY-MOTION LEDGER. Reuse all AC01+/V01+/E01+/OBJ01+ IDs declared in the still prompt. For each moving entity, specify start position, initial velocity/state, path, interaction, end position and terminal velocity/state. Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL007. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.

Define camera START as the position encoded by S008-B_FINAL. Keep a fixed lens unless an intentional optical zoom is explicitly required; default is no zoom. Pan/tilt only to retain the primary subject. Camera roll remains essentially zero except slight physically caused platform response. Stabilization is realistic: no floating gimbal drift. END camera position remains within a physically reachable path over 6 seconds and preserves the action axis.
SUBJECT MOTION / SPEED / MECHANICS. Aircraft-motion control: define a single coherent heading and flight state for every visible aircraft. For the low-level ingress sequences, use a production estimate of roughly 10–30 m AGL over open water/flat terrain and a visually credible transit range around 180–240 km/h unless the shot is landing, flaring, turning, damaged or otherwise requires a different bounded state; these values are cinematic/physical staging estimates, not claims of measured combat telemetry. Keep rotor discs physically clear: no intersecting rotor volumes, no air-show wingtip proximity, no cloned spacing. Use staggered longitudinal and lateral separation so each aircraft has wake/rotor safety margin and the viewer can read the package. Bank and pitch must correspond to the commanded turn or speed change. Door, landing-gear and troop-egress states change only for a physical reason. Rotor blur should be photographically plausible rather than frozen or turned into transparent discs. Any damaged aircraft must follow an inertial, aerodynamically plausible path and must not explode simply because it is hit.
ENTITY-MOTION LEDGER. Reuse all AC01+/V01+/E01+/OBJ01+ IDs declared in the still prompt. For each moving entity, specify start position, initial velocity/state, path, interaction, end position and terminal velocity/state. Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL008. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.

CAMERA TRAJECTORY CONTRACT. Treatment concept: Canonical three-dimensional aviation view: physically plausible real camera, clear formation geometry, moderate normal/short-telephoto lens, action axis easy to read. Use one motivated move only: stable observation, restrained pan/track or platform-coupled move selected to clarify the primary action. Define camera START as the position encoded by S009-A_FINAL. Keep a fixed lens unless an intentional optical zoom is explicitly required; default is no zoom. Pan/tilt only to retain the primary subject. Camera roll remains essentially zero except slight physically caused platform response. Stabilization is realistic: no floating gimbal drift. END camera position remains within a physically reachable path over 8 seconds and preserves the action axis.
SUBJECT MOTION / SPEED / MECHANICS. Aircraft-motion control: define a single coherent heading and flight state for every visible aircraft. For the low-level ingress sequences, use a production estimate of roughly 10–30 m AGL over open water/flat terrain and a visually credible transit range around 180–240 km/h unless the shot is landing, flaring, turning, damaged or otherwise requires a different bounded state; these values are cinematic/physical staging estimates, not claims of measured combat telemetry. Keep rotor discs physically clear: no intersecting rotor volumes, no air-show wingtip proximity, no cloned spacing. Use staggered longitudinal and lateral separation so each aircraft has wake/rotor safety margin and the viewer can read the package. Bank and pitch must correspond to the commanded turn or speed change. Door, landing-gear and troop-egress states change only for a physical reason. Rotor blur should be photographically plausible rather than frozen or turned into transparent discs. Any damaged aircraft must follow an inertial, aerodynamically plausible path and must not explode simply because it is hit.
ENTITY-MOTION LEDGER. Reuse all AC01+/V01+/E01+/OBJ01+ IDs declared in the still prompt. For each moving entity, specify start position, initial velocity/state, path, interaction, end position and terminal velocity/state. Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL009. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.
