TEMPORAL DELTA / PRIMARY EVENT. Over 8 seconds, animate only the causal change required by this beat: Mi-8 transports carry the assault echelon behind attack helicopters. The action must be readable in real time rather than compressed into a montage of unrelated events. Build a short lead-in, decisive middle action and resolved final state where possible. Do not advance into the next historical beat simply because time remains.
CAMERA TRAJECTORY CONTRACT. Treatment concept: Premium elevated/offset platform view with stable geography and restrained camera movement, designed as a high-value alternate without impossible drone proximity or orbiting. Use a premium controlled offset move or stable elevated observation; one dominant path, physically achievable, no orbiting. Define camera START as the position encoded by S009-D_FINAL. Keep a fixed lens unless an intentional optical zoom is explicitly required; default is no zoom. Pan/tilt only to retain the primary subject. Camera roll remains essentially zero except slight physically caused platform response. Stabilization is realistic: no floating gimbal drift. END camera position remains within a physically reachable path over 8 seconds and preserves the action axis.
SUBJECT MOTION / SPEED / MECHANICS. Aircraft-motion control: define a single coherent heading and flight state for every visible aircraft. For the low-level ingress sequences, use a production estimate of roughly 10–30 m AGL over open water/flat terrain and a visually credible transit range around 180–240 km/h unless the shot is landing, flaring, turning, damaged or otherwise requires a different bounded state; these values are cinematic/physical staging estimates, not claims of measured combat telemetry. Keep rotor discs physically clear: no intersecting rotor volumes, no air-show wingtip proximity, no cloned spacing. Use staggered longitudinal and lateral separation so each aircraft has wake/rotor safety margin and the viewer can read the package. Bank and pitch must correspond to the commanded turn or speed change. Door, landing-gear and troop-egress states change only for a physical reason. Rotor blur should be photographically plausible rather than frozen or turned into transparent discs. Any damaged aircraft must follow an inertial, aerodynamically plausible path and must not explode simply because it is hit.
ENTITY-MOTION LEDGER. Reuse all AC01+/V01+/E01+/OBJ01+ IDs declared in the still prompt. For each moving entity, specify start position, initial velocity/state, path, interaction, end position and terminal velocity/state. Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL009. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.

ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.

Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.

COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL014. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.

Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL014. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.

Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL015. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.

Rotor blur should be photographically plausible rather than frozen or turned into transparent discs. Any damaged aircraft must follow an inertial, aerodynamically plausible path and must not explode simply because it is hit.
ENTITY-MOTION LEDGER. Reuse all AC01+/V01+/E01+/OBJ01+ IDs declared in the still prompt. For each moving entity, specify start position, initial velocity/state, path, interaction, end position and terminal velocity/state. Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL016. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.

Use one motivated move only: stable observation, restrained pan/track or platform-coupled move selected to clarify the primary action. Define camera START as the position encoded by S017-A_FINAL. Keep a fixed lens unless an intentional optical zoom is explicitly required; default is no zoom. Pan/tilt only to retain the primary subject. Camera roll remains essentially zero except slight physically caused platform response. Stabilization is realistic: no floating gimbal drift. END camera position remains within a physically reachable path over 8 seconds and preserves the action axis.
SUBJECT MOTION / SPEED / MECHANICS. Aircraft-motion control: define a single coherent heading and flight state for every visible aircraft. For the low-level ingress sequences, use a production estimate of roughly 10–30 m AGL over open water/flat terrain and a visually credible transit range around 180–240 km/h unless the shot is landing, flaring, turning, damaged or otherwise requires a different bounded state; these values are cinematic/physical staging estimates, not claims of measured combat telemetry. Keep rotor discs physically clear: no intersecting rotor volumes, no air-show wingtip proximity, no cloned spacing. Use staggered longitudinal and lateral separation so each aircraft has wake/rotor safety margin and the viewer can read the package. Bank and pitch must correspond to the commanded turn or speed change. Door, landing-gear and troop-egress states change only for a physical reason. Rotor blur should be photographically plausible rather than frozen or turned into transparent discs. Any damaged aircraft must follow an inertial, aerodynamically plausible path and must not explode simply because it is hit.
ENTITY-MOTION LEDGER. Reuse all AC01+/V01+/E01+/OBJ01+ IDs declared in the still prompt. For each moving entity, specify start position, initial velocity/state, path, interaction, end position and terminal velocity/state. Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL017. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.

Treatment concept: Premium elevated/offset platform view with stable geography and restrained camera movement, designed as a high-value alternate without impossible drone proximity or orbiting. Use a premium controlled offset move or stable elevated observation; one dominant path, physically achievable, no orbiting. Define camera START as the position encoded by S017-D_FINAL. Keep a fixed lens unless an intentional optical zoom is explicitly required; default is no zoom. Pan/tilt only to retain the primary subject. Camera roll remains essentially zero except slight physically caused platform response. Stabilization is realistic: no floating gimbal drift. END camera position remains within a physically reachable path over 8 seconds and preserves the action axis.
SUBJECT MOTION / SPEED / MECHANICS. Aircraft-motion control: define a single coherent heading and flight state for every visible aircraft. For the low-level ingress sequences, use a production estimate of roughly 10–30 m AGL over open water/flat terrain and a visually credible transit range around 180–240 km/h unless the shot is landing, flaring, turning, damaged or otherwise requires a different bounded state; these values are cinematic/physical staging estimates, not claims of measured combat telemetry. Keep rotor discs physically clear: no intersecting rotor volumes, no air-show wingtip proximity, no cloned spacing. Use staggered longitudinal and lateral separation so each aircraft has wake/rotor safety margin and the viewer can read the package. Bank and pitch must correspond to the commanded turn or speed change. Door, landing-gear and troop-egress states change only for a physical reason. Rotor blur should be photographically plausible rather than frozen or turned into transparent discs. Any damaged aircraft must follow an inertial, aerodynamically plausible path and must not explode simply because it is hit.
ENTITY-MOTION LEDGER. Reuse all AC01+/V01+/E01+/OBJ01+ IDs declared in the still prompt. For each moving entity, specify start position, initial velocity/state, path, interaction, end position and terminal velocity/state. Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL017. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.

Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.

There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.

TEMPORAL DELTA / PRIMARY EVENT. Over 8 seconds, animate only the causal change required by this beat: Attack helicopters separate toward defensive positions; transports continue toward landing areas. The action must be readable in real time rather than compressed into a montage of unrelated events. Build a short lead-in, decisive middle action and resolved final state where possible. Do not advance into the next historical beat simply because time remains.
CAMERA TRAJECTORY CONTRACT. Treatment concept: Longer-lens compressed aviation observation from farther away, preserving relative altitude and spacing while increasing atmospheric depth and reducing perspective exaggeration. Use a restrained long-lens follow/pan from standoff; keep focal length fixed and avoid artificial push-in unless the shot contract explicitly needs one. Define camera START as the position encoded by S019-B_FINAL. Keep a fixed lens unless an intentional optical zoom is explicitly required; default is no zoom. Pan/tilt only to retain the primary subject. Camera roll remains essentially zero except slight physically caused platform response. Stabilization is realistic: no floating gimbal drift. END camera position remains within a physically reachable path over 8 seconds and preserves the action axis.
SUBJECT MOTION / SPEED / MECHANICS. Aircraft-motion control: define a single coherent heading and flight state for every visible aircraft. For the low-level ingress sequences, use a production estimate of roughly 10–30 m AGL over open water/flat terrain and a visually credible transit range around 180–240 km/h unless the shot is landing, flaring, turning, damaged or otherwise requires a different bounded state; these values are cinematic/physical staging estimates, not claims of measured combat telemetry. Keep rotor discs physically clear: no intersecting rotor volumes, no air-show wingtip proximity, no cloned spacing. Use staggered longitudinal and lateral separation so each aircraft has wake/rotor safety margin and the viewer can read the package. Bank and pitch must correspond to the commanded turn or speed change. Door, landing-gear and troop-egress states change only for a physical reason. Rotor blur should be photographically plausible rather than frozen or turned into transparent discs. Any damaged aircraft must follow an inertial, aerodynamically plausible path and must not explode simply because it is hit.
ENTITY-MOTION LEDGER. Reuse all AC01+/V01+/E01+/OBJ01+ IDs declared in the still prompt. For each moving entity, specify start position, initial velocity/state, path, interaction, end position and terminal velocity/state. Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL019. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.

NARRATION LINK (LOCKED): By around 11:00, the assault reaches the airport. Ka-52s and Mi-24s suppress Ukrainian positions while the Mi-8 transports push toward the landing areas. Two successive lifts of ten Mi-8s each put roughly three hundred Russian VDV and special-purpose troops onto Antonov.
FLOW TASK TITLE: "ANIMATE AP020-A FROM S020-A_FINAL — Mi-8s Push for the Landing Areas"
MUST KEEP / IMMUTABLE VISUAL STATE. 1) Animate exactly S020-A_FINAL and no other treatment. 2) Identity, count, equipment family, colours, airport geometry, weather/light and starting damage state are frozen from the still and canonical authorities. 3) Do not add/remove/swap aircraft, vehicles, people, weapons or structures. 4) Do not invent readable markings, tail numbers or unit badges. 5) Motion must obey inertia, contact and mechanical limits. 6) Effects have a single causal source and persist. 7) Camera behaviour must be physically achievable and must not introduce a new viewpoint that exposes unresearched surfaces. 8) End state changes only what this beat authorizes and is written to CL020.
HARD BINDING VALIDATION. Confirm numeric family  020, treatment suffix A, title, source still, continuity ledger and reference authorities all match. If the attached still is not exactly S020-A_FINAL, STOP with QC_FAIL_BINDING. AP treatments cannot cross-bind: AP020-A may not animate S020-A/B/C/D other than S020-A.
EXACT START STATE. Begin from the approved still with no visual reset. Preserve every visible entity's local ID, screen/depth position, facing, gear/door/weapon state, damage state, smoke owner, light and environmental state. The first useful frames should feel stable enough for an edit handle rather than snapping into motion from a different composition.
TEMPORAL DELTA / PRIMARY EVENT. Over 8 seconds, animate only the causal change required by this beat: Mi-8s cross airfield boundary under fire toward defensible landing zones. The action must be readable in real time rather than compressed into a montage of unrelated events. Build a short lead-in, decisive middle action and resolved final state where possible. Do not advance into the next historical beat simply because time remains.
CAMERA TRAJECTORY CONTRACT. Treatment concept: Canonical three-dimensional aviation view: physically plausible real camera, clear formation geometry, moderate normal/short-telephoto lens, action axis easy to read. Use one motivated move only: stable observation, restrained pan/track or platform-coupled move selected to clarify the primary action. Define camera START as the position encoded by S020-A_FINAL. Keep a fixed lens unless an intentional optical zoom is explicitly required; default is no zoom. Pan/tilt only to retain the primary subject. Camera roll remains essentially zero except slight physically caused platform response. Stabilization is realistic: no floating gimbal drift. END camera position remains within a physically reachable path over 8 seconds and preserves the action axis.
SUBJECT MOTION / SPEED / MECHANICS. Aircraft-motion control: define a single coherent heading and flight state for every visible aircraft. For the low-level ingress sequences, use a production estimate of roughly 10–30 m AGL over open water/flat terrain and a visually credible transit range around 180–240 km/h unless the shot is landing, flaring, turning, damaged or otherwise requires a different bounded state; these values are cinematic/physical staging estimates, not claims of measured combat telemetry. Keep rotor discs physically clear: no intersecting rotor volumes, no air-show wingtip proximity, no cloned spacing. Use staggered longitudinal and lateral separation so each aircraft has wake/rotor safety margin and the viewer can read the package. Bank and pitch must correspond to the commanded turn or speed change. Door, landing-gear and troop-egress states change only for a physical reason. Rotor blur should be photographically plausible rather than frozen or turned into transparent discs. Any damaged aircraft must follow an inertial, aerodynamically plausible path and must not explode simply because it is hit.
ENTITY-MOTION LEDGER. Reuse all AC01+/V01+/E01+/OBJ01+ IDs declared in the still prompt. For each moving entity, specify start position, initial velocity/state, path, interaction, end position and terminal velocity/state. Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL020. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.
