Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL034. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.

Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.

REFERENCE AND EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Use only the authorities declared for AP034-C bound animation for S034-C. A source-linked fact controls only the property it actually establishes. When accounts conflict, prefer visual ambiguity and record the conflict rather than merging incompatible claims. CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.

Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.

No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.

Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.
REFERENCE AND EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Use only the authorities declared for AP036-A bound animation for S036-A. A source-linked fact controls only the property it actually establishes. When a technical source describes a platform family but not the specific Hostomel aircraft, use it for geometry/performance bounds only, never as evidence for the battle loadout. When a military reconstruction supplies a time, count or route, preserve its confidence classification. When accounts conflict, prefer visual ambiguity and record the conflict rather than merging incompatible claims. The picture should communicate the narrative beat without pretending that every background individual, exact serial, weapon load, firing point or vehicle mix is known.

ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.

CAMERA TRAJECTORY CONTRACT. Treatment concept: Longer-lens compressed aviation observation from farther away, preserving relative altitude and spacing while increasing atmospheric depth and reducing perspective exaggeration. Use a restrained long-lens follow/pan from standoff; keep focal length fixed and avoid artificial push-in unless the shot contract explicitly needs one. Define camera START as the position encoded by S038-B_FINAL. Keep a fixed lens unless an intentional optical zoom is explicitly required; default is no zoom. Pan/tilt only to retain the primary subject. Camera roll remains essentially zero except slight physically caused platform response. Stabilization is realistic: no floating gimbal drift. END camera position remains within a physically reachable path over 8 seconds and preserves the action axis.
SUBJECT MOTION / SPEED / MECHANICS. Aircraft-motion control: define a single coherent heading and flight state for every visible aircraft. For the low-level ingress sequences, use a production estimate of roughly 10–30 m AGL over open water/flat terrain and a visually credible transit range around 180–240 km/h unless the shot is landing, flaring, turning, damaged or otherwise requires a different bounded state; these values are cinematic/physical staging estimates, not claims of measured combat telemetry. Keep rotor discs physically clear: no intersecting rotor volumes, no air-show wingtip proximity, no cloned spacing. Use staggered longitudinal and lateral separation so each aircraft has wake/rotor safety margin and the viewer can read the package. Bank and pitch must correspond to the commanded turn or speed change. Door, landing-gear and troop-egress states change only for a physical reason. Rotor blur should be photographically plausible rather than frozen or turned into transparent discs. Any damaged aircraft must follow an inertial, aerodynamically plausible path and must not explode simply because it is hit.
ENTITY-MOTION LEDGER. Reuse all AC01+/V01+/E01+/OBJ01+ IDs declared in the still prompt. For each moving entity, specify start position, initial velocity/state, path, interaction, end position and terminal velocity/state. Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL038. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.

No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL041. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.
REFERENCE AND EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Use only the authorities declared for AP041-D bound animation for S041-D. A source-linked fact controls only the property it actually establishes. When a technical source describes a platform family but not the specific Hostomel aircraft, use it for geometry/performance bounds only, never as evidence for the battle loadout. When a military reconstruction supplies a time, count or route, preserve its confidence classification. When accounts conflict, prefer visual ambiguity and record the conflict rather than merging incompatible claims. The picture should communicate the narrative beat without pretending that every background individual, exact serial, weapon load, firing point or vehicle mix is known.

For each moving entity, specify start position, initial velocity/state, path, interaction, end position and terminal velocity/state. Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL042. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.

Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.
REFERENCE AND EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Use only the authorities declared for AP042-C bound animation for S042-C. A source-linked fact controls only the property it actually establishes. When a technical source describes a platform family but not the specific Hostomel aircraft, use it for geometry/performance bounds only, never as evidence for the battle loadout. When a military reconstruction supplies a time, count or route, preserve its confidence classification. When accounts conflict, prefer visual ambiguity and record the conflict rather than merging incompatible claims. The picture should communicate the narrative beat without pretending that every background individual, exact serial, weapon load, firing point or vehicle mix is known.

COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.

CAMERA TRAJECTORY CONTRACT. Treatment concept: Canonical grounded documentary master at human height, readable force directions, cover and tasking, restrained shoulder/locked behaviour chosen for the beat. Use one motivated move only: stable observation, restrained pan/track or platform-coupled move selected to clarify the primary action. Define camera START as the position encoded by S044-A_FINAL. Camera roll remains essentially zero except slight physically caused platform response. Stabilization is realistic: no floating gimbal drift. END camera position remains within a physically reachable path over 8 seconds and preserves the action axis.
SUBJECT MOTION / SPEED / MECHANICS. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.

Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.

Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL044. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.

No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.

PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.
REFERENCE AND EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Use only the authorities declared for AP044-A bound animation for S044-A. A source-linked fact controls only the property it actually establishes. When a technical source describes a platform family but not the specific Hostomel aircraft, use it for geometry/performance bounds only, never as evidence for the battle loadout. When a military reconstruction supplies a time, count or route, preserve its confidence classification. When accounts conflict, prefer visual ambiguity and record the conflict rather than merging incompatible claims. The picture should communicate the narrative beat without pretending that every background individual, exact serial, weapon load, firing point or vehicle mix is known.

Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL044. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.

Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.

If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.
REFERENCE AND EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Use only the authorities declared for AP044-D bound animation for S044-D. A source-linked fact controls only the property it actually establishes. When a technical source describes a platform family but not the specific Hostomel aircraft, use it for geometry/performance bounds only, never as evidence for the battle loadout. When a military reconstruction supplies a time, count or route, preserve its confidence classification. When accounts conflict, prefer visual ambiguity and record the conflict rather than merging incompatible claims. The picture should communicate the narrative beat without pretending that every background individual, exact serial, weapon load, firing point or vehicle mix is known.

CAMERA TRAJECTORY CONTRACT. Treatment concept: Lower human/technical viewpoint that changes scale and emphasis while preserving the action axis and historical state. SUBJECT MOTION / SPEED / MECHANICS. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.

Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL045. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.
REFERENCE AND EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Use only the authorities declared for AP045-C bound animation for S045-C. A source-linked fact controls only the property it actually establishes. When a technical source describes a platform family but not the specific Hostomel aircraft, use it for geometry/performance bounds only, never as evidence for the battle loadout. When a military reconstruction supplies a time, count or route, preserve its confidence classification. When accounts conflict, prefer visual ambiguity and record the conflict rather than merging incompatible claims. The picture should communicate the narrative beat without pretending that every background individual, exact serial, weapon load, firing point or vehicle mix is known.

Over 6 seconds, animate only the causal change required by this beat: Controlled close/wide evidence of runway damage; do not imply damage alone is the sole abort cause. Do not advance into the next historical beat simply because time remains.
CAMERA TRAJECTORY CONTRACT. Treatment concept: Longer-lens compressed aviation observation from farther away, preserving relative altitude and spacing while increasing atmospheric depth and reducing perspective exaggeration. Use a restrained long-lens follow/pan from standoff; keep focal length fixed and avoid artificial push-in unless the shot contract explicitly needs one. Define camera START as the position encoded by S046-B_FINAL. Keep a fixed lens unless an intentional optical zoom is explicitly required; default is no zoom. Pan/tilt only to retain the primary subject. Camera roll remains essentially zero except slight physically caused platform response. Stabilization is realistic: no floating gimbal drift. END camera position remains within a physically reachable path over 6 seconds and preserves the action axis.
SUBJECT MOTION / SPEED / MECHANICS. Aircraft-motion control: define a single coherent heading and flight state for every visible aircraft. For the low-level ingress sequences, use a production estimate of roughly 10–30 m AGL over open water/flat terrain and a visually credible transit range around 180–240 km/h unless the shot is landing, flaring, turning, damaged or otherwise requires a different bounded state; these values are cinematic/physical staging estimates, not claims of measured combat telemetry. Keep rotor discs physically clear: no intersecting rotor volumes, no air-show wingtip proximity, no cloned spacing. Use staggered longitudinal and lateral separation so each aircraft has wake/rotor safety margin and the viewer can read the package. Bank and pitch must correspond to the commanded turn or speed change. Door, landing-gear and troop-egress states change only for a physical reason. Rotor blur should be photographically plausible rather than frozen or turned into transparent discs. Any damaged aircraft must follow an inertial, aerodynamically plausible path and must not explode simply because it is hit.
ENTITY-MOTION LEDGER. Reuse all AC01+/V01+/E01+/OBJ01+ IDs declared in the still prompt. For each moving entity, specify start position, initial velocity/state, path, interaction, end position and terminal velocity/state. Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL046. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.

SUBJECT MOTION / SPEED / MECHANICS. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.

Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.

No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.

Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. When a technical source describes a platform family but not the specific Hostomel aircraft, use it for geometry/performance bounds only, never as evidence for the battle loadout. When a military reconstruction supplies a time, count or route, preserve its confidence classification. When accounts conflict, prefer visual ambiguity and record the conflict rather than merging incompatible claims. The picture should communicate the narrative beat without pretending that every background individual, exact serial, weapon load, firing point or vehicle mix is known.

ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL051. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.

For each moving entity, specify start position, initial velocity/state, path, interaction, end position and terminal velocity/state. Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL052. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.
REFERENCE AND EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Use only the authorities declared for AP052-A bound animation for S052-A. A source-linked fact controls only the property it actually establishes. When a technical source describes a platform family but not the specific Hostomel aircraft, use it for geometry/performance bounds only, never as evidence for the battle loadout. When a military reconstruction supplies a time, count or route, preserve its confidence classification. When accounts conflict, prefer visual ambiguity and record the conflict rather than merging incompatible claims. The picture should communicate the narrative beat without pretending that every background individual, exact serial, weapon load, firing point or vehicle mix is known.
