END camera position remains within a physically reachable path over 8 seconds and preserves the action axis.
SUBJECT MOTION / SPEED / MECHANICS. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
ENTITY-MOTION LEDGER. Reuse all AC01+/V01+/E01+/OBJ01+ IDs declared in the still prompt. For each moving entity, specify start position, initial velocity/state, path, interaction, end position and terminal velocity/state. Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL052. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.
REFERENCE AND EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Use only the authorities declared for AP052-D bound animation for S052-D. A source-linked fact controls only the property it actually establishes. When a technical source describes a platform family but not the specific Hostomel aircraft, use it for geometry/performance bounds only, never as evidence for the battle loadout. When a military reconstruction supplies a time, count or route, preserve its confidence classification. When accounts conflict, prefer visual ambiguity and record the conflict rather than merging incompatible claims. The picture should communicate the narrative beat without pretending that every background individual, exact serial, weapon load, firing point or vehicle mix is known.

Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. REFERENCE AND EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Use only the authorities declared for AP053-C bound animation for S053-C. A source-linked fact controls only the property it actually establishes. When accounts conflict, prefer visual ambiguity and record the conflict rather than merging incompatible claims. COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.

REFERENCE AND EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Use only the authorities declared for AP054-B bound animation for S054-B. A source-linked fact controls only the property it actually establishes. When a technical source describes a platform family but not the specific Hostomel aircraft, use it for geometry/performance bounds only, never as evidence for the battle loadout. When a military reconstruction supplies a time, count or route, preserve its confidence classification. When accounts conflict, prefer visual ambiguity and record the conflict rather than merging incompatible claims. The picture should communicate the narrative beat without pretending that every background individual, exact serial, weapon load, firing point or vehicle mix is known.

NARRATION LINK (LOCKED): On 25 February, those ground forces reach the airport and link with the airborne troops. Armored and mechanized forces secure Antonov Airport again. Russia has recovered the airfield — but by road, not through the rapid aerial reinforcement operation intended on the first morning.
FLOW TASK TITLE: "ANIMATE AP055-A FROM S055-A_FINAL — Airport Secured Again — By Road"
MUST KEEP / IMMUTABLE VISUAL STATE. 1) Animate exactly S055-A_FINAL and no other treatment. 2) Identity, count, equipment family, colours, airport geometry, weather/light and starting damage state are frozen from the still and canonical authorities. 3) Do not add/remove/swap aircraft, vehicles, people, weapons or structures. 4) Do not invent readable markings, tail numbers or unit badges. 5) Motion must obey inertia, contact and mechanical limits. 6) Effects have a single causal source and persist. 7) Camera behaviour must be physically achievable and must not introduce a new viewpoint that exposes unresearched surfaces. 8) End state changes only what this beat authorizes and is written to CL055.
HARD BINDING VALIDATION. Confirm numeric family  055, treatment suffix A, title, source still, continuity ledger and reference authorities all match. If the attached still is not exactly S055-A_FINAL, STOP with QC_FAIL_BINDING. AP treatments cannot cross-bind: AP055-A may not animate S055-A/B/C/D other than S055-A.
EXACT START STATE. Begin from the approved still with no visual reset. Preserve every visible entity's local ID, screen/depth position, facing, gear/door/weapon state, damage state, smoke owner, light and environmental state. The first useful frames should feel stable enough for an edit handle rather than snapping into motion from a different composition.
TEMPORAL DELTA / PRIMARY EVENT. Over 6 seconds, animate only the causal change required by this beat: Russian possession of Antonov re-established by ground link-up; runway still not an active Il-76 bridge. The action must be readable in real time rather than compressed into a montage of unrelated events. Build a short lead-in, decisive middle action and resolved final state where possible. Do not advance into the next historical beat simply because time remains.
CAMERA TRAJECTORY CONTRACT. Treatment concept: Canonical director treatment balancing geography, subject readability and editorial continuity with a physically plausible real camera. Use one motivated move only: stable observation, restrained pan/track or platform-coupled move selected to clarify the primary action. Define camera START as the position encoded by S055-A_FINAL. Keep a fixed lens unless an intentional optical zoom is explicitly required; default is no zoom. Pan/tilt only to retain the primary subject. Camera roll remains essentially zero except slight physically caused platform response. Stabilization is realistic: no floating gimbal drift. END camera position remains within a physically reachable path over 6 seconds and preserves the action axis.
SUBJECT MOTION / SPEED / MECHANICS. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
ENTITY-MOTION LEDGER. Reuse all AC01+/V01+/E01+/OBJ01+ IDs declared in the still prompt. For each moving entity, specify start position, initial velocity/state, path, interaction, end position and terminal velocity/state. Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL055. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.
REFERENCE AND EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Use only the authorities declared for AP055-A bound animation for S055-A. A source-linked fact controls only the property it actually establishes. When a technical source describes a platform family but not the specific Hostomel aircraft, use it for geometry/performance bounds only, never as evidence for the battle loadout. When a military reconstruction supplies a time, count or route, preserve its confidence classification. When accounts conflict, prefer visual ambiguity and record the conflict rather than merging incompatible claims. The picture should communicate the narrative beat without pretending that every background individual, exact serial, weapon load, firing point or vehicle mix is known.

Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL058. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.

Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. REFERENCE AND EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Use only the authorities declared for AP058-C bound animation for S058-C. A source-linked fact controls only the property it actually establishes. Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL059. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.
REFERENCE AND EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Use only the authorities declared for AP059-B bound animation for S059-B. A source-linked fact controls only the property it actually establishes. When a technical source describes a platform family but not the specific Hostomel aircraft, use it for geometry/performance bounds only, never as evidence for the battle loadout. When a military reconstruction supplies a time, count or route, preserve its confidence classification. When accounts conflict, prefer visual ambiguity and record the conflict rather than merging incompatible claims. The picture should communicate the narrative beat without pretending that every background individual, exact serial, weapon load, firing point or vehicle mix is known.

COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.

When accounts conflict, prefer visual ambiguity and record the conflict rather than merging incompatible claims. The picture should communicate the narrative beat without pretending that every background individual, exact serial, weapon load, firing point or vehicle mix is known.

CAMERA TRAJECTORY CONTRACT. Treatment concept: Grounded low or near-surface observation angle with strong foreground scale cue; aircraft crossing laterally or diagonally while the action axis remains unchanged. Use grounded operator behaviour: locked or minimal shoulder correction, with human-scale parallax and no high-frequency combat shake. Define camera START as the position encoded by S061-C_FINAL. Keep a fixed lens unless an intentional optical zoom is explicitly required; default is no zoom. Pan/tilt only to retain the primary subject. Camera roll remains essentially zero except slight physically caused platform response. Stabilization is realistic: no floating gimbal drift. END camera position remains within a physically reachable path over 6 seconds and preserves the action axis.
SUBJECT MOTION / SPEED / MECHANICS. Aircraft-motion control: define a single coherent heading and flight state for every visible aircraft. For the low-level ingress sequences, use a production estimate of roughly 10–30 m AGL over open water/flat terrain and a visually credible transit range around 180–240 km/h unless the shot is landing, flaring, turning, damaged or otherwise requires a different bounded state; these values are cinematic/physical staging estimates, not claims of measured combat telemetry. Keep rotor discs physically clear: no intersecting rotor volumes, no air-show wingtip proximity, no cloned spacing. Use staggered longitudinal and lateral separation so each aircraft has wake/rotor safety margin and the viewer can read the package. Bank and pitch must correspond to the commanded turn or speed change. Door, landing-gear and troop-egress states change only for a physical reason. Rotor blur should be photographically plausible rather than frozen or turned into transparent discs. Any damaged aircraft must follow an inertial, aerodynamically plausible path and must not explode simply because it is hit.
ENTITY-MOTION LEDGER. Reuse all AC01+/V01+/E01+/OBJ01+ IDs declared in the still prompt. For each moving entity, specify start position, initial velocity/state, path, interaction, end position and terminal velocity/state. Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL061. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.
RECOMMENDED EDIT HANDLES. Preserve approximately 0.5–1.0 seconds of compositionally controlled lead-in where feasible and a clean resolved tail. QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.
QC ACCEPTANCE. Pass only if binding is exact, subject count never changes, motion is physically causal, every moving entity follows the same identity, aircraft separation and rotor clearances remain safe, camera trajectory is physically possible, no AI morphing/duplication appears, effects have owners, light/weather remain continuous, terminal state is usable, and audio does not obscure future narration. Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.

Pan/tilt only to retain the primary subject. Camera roll remains essentially zero except slight physically caused platform response. Stabilization is realistic: no floating gimbal drift. END camera position remains within a physically reachable path over 8 seconds and preserves the action axis.
SUBJECT MOTION / SPEED / MECHANICS. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.

Background entities not assigned motion remain static or exhibit only physically natural micro-motion. Never allow the model to reinterpret “the helicopters,” “the troops” or “the vehicles” as a different number/group during animation.
CONTACT / HUMAN TASKING. Ground-force control: when manageable, enumerate every clearly visible person; otherwise use explicit subgroups whose counts reconcile to the visible total. Assign each group a task, posture, travel direction, cover relation, weapon state and nearest-neighbour spacing. Nobody stands decoratively in exposed areas when the tactical situation calls for cover. Hands contact weapons, radios, ammunition or equipment for a reason. Opposing forces must not be accidentally intermingled. Avoid dense AI melee; decompose combat into approach, observation, fire from cover, movement, reaction and consequence. No one fires through friendly bodies, walls or vehicle hulls. Wounded/dead figures are not used for spectacle and gore is excluded.
COMBAT / EFFECT TIMING. Combat-effects control: every muzzle flash, rocket launch, flare, impact, fire and smoke plume has one identifiable owner/source. Effects appear only at the moment required by the shot and persist causally afterwards. Smoke ages, expands and drifts with the same wind field rather than teleporting. Do not use universal fireballs, shockwave rings, laser-like tracers, endless visible bullets, synchronized explosions or arbitrary debris. Artillery effects are localized and physically proportionate; runway damage remains bounded and does not visually imply that cratering alone caused the Il-76 abort. Rotor wash affects loose grass, damp grit, fabric and light debris near the aircraft but does not create desert-scale dust clouds on wet winter ground. If the shot has no firing/impact event, do not add one for excitement. If it does, establish the source before consequence, show only the required transient, and carry residue/smoke/damage into the end state. Ordinary projectiles are not visible unless size, tracer type, distance, exposure and evidence justify them.
ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE. Rotor wash, vehicle movement, blast impulse, smoke, grass, branches and loose debris respond only to nearby physical forces. The same wind field applies through the clip. Damp ground does not spontaneously become a dust storm. Smoke does not reverse direction. Camera shake occurs only when the camera/operator/platform could physically receive the impulse, and recovery is quick and restrained.
AUDIO / FOLEY STRATEGY. Generate or plan native foley appropriate to the shot but no baked narration. Helicopter clips use layered rotor blade slap/engine/transmission presence scaled by distance, wind and doppler; aircraft pass-bys use plausible turbine/airflow; ground shots use footsteps, kit movement, distant engines, gun mechanisms, reports and reverberation appropriate to location. Artillery reports and impacts are separated by realistic distance/delay where audible. Do not create a constant wall of gunfire. Preserve editorial room for final voiceover and score.
EXACT TERMINAL STATE. End after the stated beat has materially changed the scene, with subjects in a stable, physically plausible continuation state. Record new positions, headings, speed states, door/gear/weapon state, troop group zones, damage, wrecks, crater additions, smoke age and control-state changes into CL062. Do not erase objects merely because they exit frame. The next shot may omit them by framing but not delete them from history.
FROZEN / IMMOBILE PROPERTIES. Canonical identity, platform geometry, camouflage/paint, factual markings, airport structures, runway axis, landscape geometry, weather regime and unrelated background assets remain unchanged. No morphing vehicle panels, breathing armour, rubber rotor blades, liquid concrete, changing building windows or spontaneous costume/equipment changes.

QC selects the actual IN/OUT; do not force a universal trim. The strongest contiguous segment should carry the locked narration beat without needing explanatory on-screen text.

Any identity/count/geometry/binding failure is structural and requires repair rather than acceptance.
PROHIBITED MOTION / FAILURE CONCEPTS. Reject and regenerate for: wrong aircraft/weapon/vehicle family; accidental modernized subtype; wrong visible count when count-critical; mirrored airport; runway axis reversal; impossible rotor overlap; duplicated aircraft or troops; opposite headings inside one formation; floating people; fused weapons; broken anatomy; impossible hands; random fireballs; excessive tracers; fake UI; captions; watermarks; arbitrary flags; invented serials; modern post-2022 equipment; over-saturated game-engine look; glossy plastic materials; impossible camera orbit; unexplained state reset; smoke without an owner; crater migration; or any visual claim stronger than the evidence register.
Continuity control: inherit permanent geometry and identity from the listed canonical A-assets and inherit temporary damage, smoke, wetness, light, troop location and control-state from the declared continuity ledger. Objects that leave frame remain alive in the ledger. A damaged aircraft does not later return undamaged unless a different explicit aircraft identity is used. A crater, wreck, smoke source or burning object cannot move between shots. A disputed historical detail remains visually non-specific in later close views; increased camera proximity does not authorize invented serials, unit badges, exact launcher subtype, tail number, crew identity, aircraft regiment or exact ground-force ORBAT.
Forensic execution audit: before release, re-read the entire prompt as a conflict linter. There must be exactly one current value for identity, date/time, visible count, ordering/grouping, operational state, weather, light direction, camera side, camera height/distance, lens concept, heading/travel direction, formation spacing, start state, continuity state and terminal state. If the prompt contains competing instructions, resolve them before generation. Ask what high-consequence decision the model would still need to invent; if the answer includes identity, count, technical configuration, spatial orientation, human tasking, terrain/site geometry, camera geometry, lighting, text or continuity, the prompt is not complete. Incidental scratches, natural folds, tiny gravel, non-critical dirt distribution and small stochastic variations in mist/smoke texture may remain model interpretation.
REFERENCE AND EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Use only the authorities declared for AP062-B bound animation for S062-B. A source-linked fact controls only the property it actually establishes. When a technical source describes a platform family but not the specific Hostomel aircraft, use it for geometry/performance bounds only, never as evidence for the battle loadout. When a military reconstruction supplies a time, count or route, preserve its confidence classification. When accounts conflict, prefer visual ambiguity and record the conflict rather than merging incompatible claims. The picture should communicate the narrative beat without pretending that every background individual, exact serial, weapon load, firing point or vehicle mix is known.

15.1 Music doctrine
Score supports geography, momentum and reversals without glorifying violence. Early rotor/engine rhythm can provide propulsion; the Il-76 threat may widen the harmonic field; Ukrainian counterattack/abort should become more tense and less triumphant; the late airport/Mriya sequence slows for consequence; the final road-to-Kyiv beat ends unresolved. Avoid heroic national leitmotifs that turn the documentary into advocacy. Silence or reduced score is acceptable around key causal reveals.

======================================================================
APPENDIX B — GOLD-STANDARD DOCUMENTARY SCRIPT REFERENCE
BATTLE OF NORFOLK — NARRATION-READY EXAMPLE
======================================================================

PURPOSE OF THIS APPENDIX:
This script is included as a stylistic calibration example for concise, chronological, narration-ready historical documentary writing. Learn from its clarity, pacing, factual density, visuality, spoken-language structure and pronunciation handling. Do not reuse its subject matter in unrelated projects.

----- BEGIN NORFOLK SCRIPT REFERENCE -----
The 26th of February 1991.

Night falls over southern Iraq.

Ahead of the United States Army's First Infantry Division - the Big Red One - lies what remains of one of Saddam Hussein's most powerful formations:

the Republican Guard's Tah-wah-KAL-nah Mechanized Division.

During the previous two days, the First Infantry Division has breached prepared Iraqi defensive positions. Now it is ordered forward again.

Its objective is a broad stretch of desert designated Objective Norfolk, around the IP-sah Pipeline Road, desert tracks and a large Iraqi supply area.

There are almost no landmarks.

Rain, dust and darkness make navigation difficult.

And somewhere ahead, Iraqi tanks and infantry fighting vehicles are waiting.

Late on the 26th of February, M-one-A-one Abrams tanks and M-two Bradley fighting vehicles begin moving east through the darkness.

Their crews see much of the battlefield through thermal sights.

Hot engines and vehicles appear as bright shapes against the black landscape.

Then Iraqi armour begins appearing ahead.

The first shots tear through the night.

Abrams crews identify Iraqi tanks through their thermal sights and fire one-hundred-and-twenty-millimetre rounds.

Bradleys engage lighter armour and fighting positions with twenty-five-millimetre cannon and TOW anti-tank missiles.

Iraqi tanks and anti-tank teams return fire.

For the American crews, the battle quickly becomes a succession of targets appearing out of the darkness.

A thermal image.

A turret.

A muzzle flash.

Then another vehicle.

The Iraqi defenses are dense.

American units are pushing into positions held by the Tah-wah-KAL-nah Division and elements of Iraq's Twelfth Armored Division.

One of the formations driving into them is Task Force Two Thirty-Four Armor, commanded by Lieutenant Colonel Gregory FAHN-teh-noh.

Nearly a thousand soldiers move forward with Abrams tanks, Bradleys, engineers, mortar crews, observers and support vehicles.

Then they run into alerted Iraqi heavy forces.

The night becomes chaotic.

American formations cross Iraqi positions faster than some crews realise they are there.

Some Iraqi tanks are dug in.

Infantry and anti-tank teams remain close to the American advance.

Vehicles appear from unexpected directions.

Burning wrecks and muzzle flashes punctuate the darkness while dust and smoke make navigation even harder.

But the thermal sights give many American crews a major advantage.

Tank commanders acquire Iraqi tanks and infantry fighting vehicles before the Iraqi crews can spot them.

Abrams crews fire into the darkness.

Bradleys engage with cannon and anti-tank missiles.

The task force keeps moving.

Again and again, Iraqi vehicles and fighting positions appear in front of it.

Again and again, the formation fires and pushes through.

By now, the battle is no longer a clean advance.

Units become mixed together.

Radio traffic is heavy.

Positions are difficult to judge.

Friendly vehicles sometimes appear unexpectedly through the smoke and thermal haze.

Several friendly-fire incidents occur during the confused night fighting.

Still, the advance continues.

Task Force 2-34 alone will be credited with destroying approximately 70 Iraqi armoured vehicles, about two dozen trucks and an undetermined number of enemy infantry, while capturing 728 Iraqi soldiers.

Across the wider battle, the scale is far larger.

The First Infantry Division's attack destroys two Iraqi brigades and penetrates positions belonging to both the Republican Guard and other Iraqi forces.

The fighting associated with the division's attack results in the destruction of nearly 300 Iraqi armoured vehicles.

By around zero-zero-thirty on the 27th of February, the division's two attacking brigades have pushed beyond the Seventy-Three Easting battle area.

Over the next several hours they drive across Objective Norfolk.

The Tah-wah-KAL-nah Division has already been hit hard by the Second Armored Cavalry Regiment.

Now the Big Red One pushes through the remaining Iraqi positions.

Iraqi soldiers surrender in large numbers.

Others abandon damaged vehicles or attempt to withdraw.

By dawn, the First Infantry Division controls Objective Norfolk.

Only then does the scale of the night battle become visible.

Wrecked tanks.

Burned-out B-M-Ps.

Abandoned trucks.

Prisoners moving toward American lines.

One of Iraq's elite Republican Guard formations has been battered apart by successive attacks.

The Battle of Norfolk has been fought largely in darkness, dust and confusion.

And in that darkness, one American advantage becomes brutally clear:

through thermal sights, many U.S. crews can see and engage Iraqi armour before the Iraqi crews can see them.

----- END NORFOLK SCRIPT REFERENCE -----
